In the online A/B test, GenRec raised the **short-term homepage engagement metric by +0.115%** (average treatment effect against the production model), with **p = 3.1 × 10⁻¹⁰**. The paper marks this as statistically significant (Figure 3, p. 6).

- **Setup:** The test focused on key batch-compute surfaces and ran on about 10% of Netflix traffic for 4 weeks (pp. 6–7). It used a low-data, low-signals configuration of the Phase-2 GenRec model (p. 6).
- **Long-term metric:** In the same figure, the long-term core metric rose by +0.006% with p = 0.025, also significant. The text calls this "statistically meaningful at Netflix scale" (p. 6).

One caveat: I read these numbers from the text layer of Figure 3, where the chart's labels are jumbled. I matched +0.115% / p = 3.1 × 10⁻¹⁰ to the short-term panel for two reasons. Those labels sit on that panel's 0–0.20% axis, and the body text confirms that +0.006% belongs to the core (long-term) metric (p. 6).
